summary: Self-improving ML experimentation loop released March 7, 2026. Agent iterates changes, runs bounded experiments, commits only improvements. 700 experiments in 2 days, 20 additive improvements retained.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — 'keep improvements, revert failures' pattern is interesting for remediation retry, but the core is RL-style training loops (disqualified red flag). HID-186 covers partial retry more appropriately.

summary: Heterogeneous multi-agent memory architecture: multiple assistant agents maintain uncompressed episodic contexts; master agent orchestrates global planning. Replaces destructive context compression with reconstruction.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly maps to run-outcome episodic memory gap, but HID-188 already tracks 'inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts'. The E-mem paper could strengthen HID-188 as a reference, but no new issue needed.

summary: LangGraph reached v1.0 in late 2025, now dominant enterprise orchestration framework. Graph-based architecture with audit trails, rollback points. Surpassed CrewAI in GitHub stars in early 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses an explicit deterministic state machine rather than a graph model. LangGraph's audit-trail and rollback patterns are conceptually adjacent but not directly adoptable without architecture changes.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel merge)
summary: Microsoft consolidated AutoGen and Semantic Kernel into Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 on April 3, 2026. Legacy AutoGen repo is now in maintenance mode.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Claude Code CLI as its runtime, not AutoGen/Semantic Kernel. Framework-level consolidation has no direct impact on AgentForge's architecture.

summary: Karpathy coined 'agentic engineering' in February 2026 covering spec design, diff review, and eval loops as the core methodology for building reliable agent systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already implements spec (plan) design and diff review (AIReview stage). Eval loops are the gap but too abstract for a single implementable issue; no verified gap beyond what HID-135 (acceptance-test harness) covers.

source: Hierarchical Memory Orchestration for Personalized Persistent Agents
summary: Proposes hierarchical multi-level memory orchestration (short-term, episodic, semantic) for personalizing persistent agent behavior across sessions. Memory accuracy improvements of ~26%.
relevanceToAgentForge: High thematically — but HID-188 already tracks run-outcome episodic memory. The skill distillation system (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts) covers semantic memory. No new gap identified.

source: CrewAI 2026 benchmarks and token overhead analysis
summary: 2026 benchmarks show CrewAI produces ~18% token overhead vs LangGraph for equivalent multi-agent tasks. Role-based crew orchestration with moderate efficiency tradeoffs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses fixed agent-to-stage mapping (not role-based crews). Token overhead awareness is relevant to HID-163 (cost telemetry) but doesn't add new capability beyond what's already tracked.
